paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the student union of your university is collecting opinions on improving its work for the coming year. You are now to write a response by suggesting how it can better enrich student life. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您所在大学的学生会正在收集关于改进来年工作的意见。您现在需要写一份回复，建议如何更好地丰富学生生活。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: People tend to want as many choices as possible. They believe this will maximize their 26 of making the best decision. But research shows that, when it comes to actually making a 27 from all of these choices, people can become 28 and avoid making a decision altogether. Even worse, when people finally do decide, they are generally less satisfied with their decision and feel more regretful over whatever choice they made.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们往往想要尽可能多的选择。他们相信这将最大限度地提高他们做出最佳决定的机会。但研究表明，当真正从所有这些选择中做出选择时，人们可能会感到困惑并完全避免做出决定。更糟糕的是，当人们最终做出决定时，他们通常对自己的决定不太满意，并对自己做出的任何选择感到更加后悔。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why does this happen? Research shows that when people choose from many options, they 29 more in the decision, but feel less confident in their ability to decide well. In other words, when we are 30 with more choices, making the “right” or “correct” decision begins to feel more 31 and, at the same time, more difficult to do. This may contribute to the deep fear that we will make the wrong decision.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么会出现这种情况？研究表明，当人们从多种选择中进行选择时，他们会在决策上投入更多，但对自己做出正确决策的能力缺乏信心。换句话说，当我们面临更多选择时，做出“正确”或“正确”的决定开始变得更加重要，同时也变得更加困难。这可能会加深我们对自己会做出错误决定的恐惧。

paragraphs.sourceText: How can we solve this problem? I believe this fear could be tempered by putting decisions into perspective. It might help to remember that many of the choices you make, such as what to have for lunch, will not 32 much in the future and that, even more important choices, like accepting a new job, can 33 be changed. It could also help to 34 these situations with clear guidelines and ideas of what you want from the 35 of options, which can narrow the possible choices, and also make you more confident about your ability to make the right decision.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们该如何解决这个问题呢？我相信通过正确看待决策可以缓解这种恐惧。记住，您所做的许多选择（例如午餐吃什么）在未来不会有太大影响，甚至更重要的选择（例如接受新工作）最终都可以改变，这可能会有所帮助。它还可以帮助您在进入这些情况时提供明确的指导方针和您想要从选项范围中获得什么的想法，这可以缩小可能的选择范围，并使您对自己做出正确决定的能力更有信心。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The battle over bike lanes needs a mindset shift
paragraphs.translationZh: 自行车道之争需要转变心态

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Five years ago, the city of Queens, New York, announced that it would be putting bike lanes onto a stretch of Skillman Ave — and removing 116 parking spots. Cyclists loved the plan, but local business owners got very angry. Taking out those parking spots, as they argued at protests and in letters to the city council, would ruin stores and restaurants along Skillman. “Parking here is already a nightmare,” one shouted at a protest rally.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 五年前，纽约皇后区宣布将在 Skillman 大道上修建自行车道，并取消 116 个停车位。骑自行车的人喜欢这个计划，但当地企业主却非常生气。正如他们在抗议活动和给市议会的信中所主张的那样，取消这些停车位将毁掉斯基尔曼沿线的商店和餐馆。 “在这里停车已经是一场噩梦，”有人在抗议集会上喊道。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But the bike lanes were a done deal, and soon they were in place. Early this year, Jesse Coburn — an investigative writer with Streetsblog New York — wondered whether those predictions of economic collapse came true. So he asked the city’s Department of Finance to give him a few years’ worth of sales figures for that stretch of Skillman Ave. How had the businesses on that street fared?
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但自行车道已经敲定了，很快就到位了。今年年初，纽约 Streetsblog 的调查作家杰西·科伯恩 (Jesse Coburn) 想知道这些经济崩溃的预测是否成真。因此，他要求市财政部提供斯基尔曼大道那段几年的销售数据。那条街上的企业表现如何？

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Quite well, it turns out. In the year after the bike lanes arrived, businesses on Skillman saw sales rise by 12 percent, compared to 3 percent for Queens in general. What’s more, that section of road saw new businesses open, while Queens overall had a net loss.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 事实证明，很好。自行车道建成后的一年里，斯基尔曼的企业销售额增长了 12%，而皇后区的整体销售额增长了 3%。更重要的是，该路段有新的企业开业，而皇后区整体出现净亏损。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The thing is, the actual merchants along Skillman? They didn’t believe it. When Coburn spoke to them and described what he’d found, only a few store owners admitted the lanes had helped. Many still insisted the lanes were killing their part of the city. And emotions ran hot: Someone scattered tacks (大头钉) on the bike lane.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 问题是，斯基尔曼沿线的实际商人？他们不相信。当科伯恩与他们交谈并描述他的发现时，只有少数店主承认这些车道起到了帮助作用。许多人仍然坚称这些小巷正在扼杀他们所在的城市。人们情绪激动：有人在自行车道上散落了大头钉。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) This little story turns out to be a fascinating glimpse at the challenges cities face as they try to update their urban infrastructure — to clean up the air, reduce greenhouse emissions, and speed up travel by making towns more bike-friendly. There’s a rising amount of data showing that installing bike lanes and making streets more pedestrian-friendly boosts the economic fortunes of a place. Removing cars and parking spots works. But the folks who run local businesses simply aren’t convinced, even when their own street performs. Given that sort of mess, can political fights over bike lanes ever end?
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 这个小故事令人着迷地一瞥了城市在尝试更新城市基础设施时所面临的挑战——净化空气、减少温室气体排放，以及通过让城镇更适合骑自行车来加快出行速度。越来越多的数据表明，安装自行车道和使街道更加适合行人可以促进一个地方的经济发展。拆除汽车和停车位是可行的。但经营当地企业的人们根本不相信，即使他们自己的街道表现良好。鉴于这种混乱，围绕自行车道的政治斗争能结束吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: F) In 2013, researchers at New York City’s Department of Transportation studied seven stretches of road that had installed bike lanes or created pedestrian-friendly areas. The city analyzed the data for businesses along those routes and found that by the third year, sales grew faster on five of the streets than in the district overall, on average — up to five times faster, in fact.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 2013 年，纽约市交通部的研究人员研究了七段安装了自行车道或创建了步行友好区的道路。该市分析了这些路线沿线企业的数据，发现到了第三年，其中五条街道的平均销售额增长速度比整个地区的增长速度还要快，事实上，速度快了五倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Beyond New York, a survey of research from 23 cities found that bike lanes and pedestrian-friendly design didn’t hurt local retail and food stores. (“Fears of disastrous consequences for local businesses are unfounded,” the researchers concluded.) More recent work has shown roughly the same.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 除了纽约之外，一项针对 23 个城市的研究调查发现，自行车道和步行友好型设计并没有损害当地的零售店和食品店。 （研究人员得出的结论是：“对当地企业遭受灾难性后果的担忧是没有根据的。”）最近的研究也显示出大致相同的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) The truth is that in fairly dense areas, bikes are more efficient at moving people around. You might lose one car driver’s business — but you gain shoppers who now can arrive more easily on bikes. “Cyclists and pedestrians are consumers too,” notes Professor Susan Handy. Plus, streets redesigned for bikes and pedestrians tend to become more pleasant places to hang around, so “in a lot of cases, that’s created much nicer environments that are really good for those businesses.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H）事实是，在相当密集的地区，自行车在运送人员方面更有效。您可能会失去一名汽车司机的生意，但您会赢得现在可以更轻松地骑自行车到达的购物者。 “骑自行车的人和行人也是消费者，”苏珊·汉迪教授指出。此外，为自行车和行人重新设计的街道往往会成为更宜人的闲逛场所，因此“在很多情况下，这创造了更好的环境，对这些企业来说确实有好处。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Mom-and-pop shops are usually pretty quick at recognizing situations that will help their bottom lines. So why the blind spot here? Perhaps it’s that attention focuses on horror stories — and some merchants do get hit when bike lanes come in.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 夫妻店通常很快就能识别出有助于盈利的情况。那么为什么这里有盲点呢？也许人们的注意力集中在恐怖故事上——而当自行车道出现时，一些商人确实受到了打击。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) I spoke to Cindy Hughes, a hairdresser (理发师) in Cambridge, Massachusetts. She said business fell by at least 40 percent when the city removed nearby parking to put in a bike lane. The majority of her customers drive, with many coming from nearby towns. Only a very few have shifted to cycling, and even those almost certainly won’t cycle in Boston’s snowy winters. So while Hughes supports bike lanes — “cyclists deserve to be safe” — she sees the parking loss as an existential risk. “Look, 90 percent of my customers drive,” she told me. “For our business, the bike lanes are way worse than Covid was.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 我采访了马萨诸塞州剑桥市的理发师辛迪·休斯 (Cindy Hughes)。她说，当市政府拆除附近的停车场并修建自行车道后，生意至少下降了 40%。她的大多数顾客都是开车的，其中许多来自附近的城镇。只有极少数人转向骑自行车，即使是那些人也几乎肯定不会在波士顿下雪的冬天骑自行车。因此，尽管休斯支持自行车道——“骑自行车的人应该安全”——但她认为停车位的减少是一种生存风险。 “看，我 90% 的顾客都开车，”她告诉我。 “对于我们的业务来说，自行车道的情况比新冠疫情还要糟糕得多。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) For others, the pushback is cultural, says Henry Grabar, a writer for the Slate Magazine. Small business owners are frequently drivers who commute from other parts of the city by car, Grabar points out. They’re also often longtime locals. “They tend to be people with deep roots in the city, who have hung around since before the neighborhood became what it is today,” he adds. Driving around town in a car is so normal to them that cycling seems weird and unusual — despite its boost from Covid, when bike sales exploded by 75 percent.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 《Slate》杂志的撰稿人亨利·格拉巴尔 (Henry Grabar) 表示，对于其他人来说，这种抵制是文化方面的。格拉巴尔指出，小企业主经常是开车从城市其他地方上下班的司机。他们通常也是本地人。 “他们往往是在城市扎根很深的人，早在这个社区变成今天的样子之前就已经在这里生活了，”他补充道。开车在城里兜风对他们来说太平常了，而骑自行车却显得怪异和不寻常——尽管它受到了新冠疫情的推动，自行车销量猛增了 75%。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Psychology beats all! Who knew, right? The fierce divide between store owners and bike-lane advocates seems similar to our larger culture wars over climate change. If we’ve learned anything about culture wars, it’s that data isn’t much good at changing minds.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 心理学胜过一切！谁知道，对吧？商店老板和自行车道倡导者之间的激烈分歧似乎类似于我们围绕气候变化展开的更大的文化战争。如果说我们从文化战争中学到了什么的话，那就是数据并不能很好地改变人们的想法。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) When Janette Sadik-Khan was the head of New York City’s Transportation Department back in the early 2000s, she oversaw a rollout (推出) of bike lanes — and got angry blowback from residents and business owners who claimed there weren’t enough cyclists to justify installing lanes. Now, she notes ironically, the lanes are so full of activity that opponents have turned to claiming the problem is the opposite: There are too many cyclists getting in the way of cars.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 2000 年代初，珍妮特·萨迪克·汗 (Janette Sadik-Khan) 担任纽约市交通局局长时，她负责监督自行车道的推出，但遭到了居民和企业主的愤怒反击，他们声称没有足够的骑自行车者来证明安装自行车道的合理性。她讽刺地指出，现在车道上的活动如此之多，以至于反对者转而声称问题恰恰相反：骑自行车的人太多了，挡住了汽车的道。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Maybe bike lanes will always be charged with emotion, until enough of the public is finally concerned about climate change — and it seems reckless (鲁莽的) to not have them.
paragraphs.translationZh: N）也许自行车道永远都会充满情感，直到足够多的公众最终担心气候变化——而没有自行车道似乎是鲁莽的。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Crises, after all, have a way of opening people’s eyes to possibilities. During Covid, restaurants and cafés lost so much business that cities nationwide began allowing them to build curbside seating areas where people could sit, safely, in the open air. It greatly reduced parking — but because, well, shop owners didn’t see any way around it. Customers loved the outdoor seating so much that cities are making it permanent: A New York City study of several streets closed during Covid found storeowners making more than before, and diners enjoying the outdoor lifestyle. If data won’t change minds, customers might.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 毕竟，危机可以让人们看到可能性。在新冠疫情期间，餐馆和咖啡馆失去了如此多的生意，以至于全国各地的城市开始允许他们建造路边座位区，人们可以安全地坐在露天。它大大减少了停车位——但因为，好吧，店主没有想到任何解决办法。顾客非常喜欢户外座位，以至于城市正在将其永久化：纽约市对新冠期间关闭的几条街道进行的一项研究发现，店主的收入比以前更高，食客也享受户外生活方式。如果数据不会改变想法，那么客户可能会改变想法。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. An increasing amount of data indicates that installing bike lanes raises local business revenues.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 越来越多的数据表明，安装自行车道可以增加当地商业收入。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. According to a magazine writer, some small business owners’ resistance to bike lanes arises from cultural factors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 据一位杂志撰稿人称，一些小企业主对自行车道的抵制源于文化因素。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. A stretch of Skillman Ave witnessed not only a big increase in sales but also the opening of new businesses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. Skillman Ave 的一段路段不仅销售额大幅增长，而且新店开业。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. When people have no way out in crises, they are more likely to embrace changes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39、当人们在危机中无路可走时，他们就更有可能拥抱变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. According to one survey, city design with bike lanes and pedestrian space did not negatively impact local businesses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 根据一项调查，设有自行车道和步行空间的城市设计并未对当地企业产生负面影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Despite increased business activity on Skillman Ave, many store owners insisted the bike lanes were destroying their area.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 尽管 Skillman 大道上的商业活动有所增加，但许多店主坚称自行车道正在破坏他们的区域。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. In a war of culture, data does not help much in changing people’s minds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 在文化战争中，数据对于改变人们的想法没有多大帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. A businesswoman said her business dropped sharply when parking space gave way to a bike lane, because most of her customers came by car.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 一位女商人说，当停车位被自行车道取代时，她的生意急剧下降，因为她的大多数顾客都是开车来的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Local business owners on Skillman Ave argued that their businesses would be ruined when parking spots were replaced by bike lanes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. Skillman Ave 的当地企业主认为，当停车位被自行车道取代时，他们的生意就会被毁掉。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. People may find it more pleasant to wander around streets redesigned for cycling and walking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 人们可能会发现在重新设计的自行车和步行街道上漫步会更愉快。

For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: All living organisms on Earth are exposed to a 24-hour day-night cycle. This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day. Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health. For example, eating at night can lead to weight gain over time because food intake at night leads to increased fat storage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 地球上的所有生物体都处于 24 小时昼夜循环之中。这个循环就是人们晚上休息、白天活跃的原因。因此，所有人体功能也遵循这种日常节律，运动或食物摄入等行为的时间可以显着影响您的健康。例如，随着时间的推移，夜间进食会导致体重增加，因为夜间进食会导致脂肪储存增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many drug targets in the body follow a 24-hour cycle, too. This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period. Because how the body responds to a drug can differ depending on the time it is taken, it logically follows that taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects.
paragraphs.translationZh: 体内的许多药物靶标也遵循 24 小时周期。这意味着药物旨在修饰的特定蛋白质在 24 小时内可能会对药物产生不同的反应。由于身体对药物的反应会根据服药时间的不同而有所不同，因此从逻辑上讲，在特定时间服药有助于提高药物的有效性并减少不必要的副作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it. There are two main reasons for that oversight. First, many physicians are not aware that some drugs work better during a specific time of the day. And second, most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle. Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当医生为人们开药时，他们很少考虑服药的最佳时间。造成这种疏忽的主要原因有两个。首先，许多医生并不知道某些药物在一天中的特定时间效果更好。其次，大多数药物尚未针对 24 小时周期内可能产生的不同效果进行研究。因此，患者被要求在早上或晚上服用大多数药物，主要是为了确保依从性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Over 50 years ago, researchers found that the cholesterol drug simvastatin is more effective at lowering cholesterol levels when taken at night rather than during the day. This is because the liver enzyme (酶) these drugs target is more active at night.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50 多年前，研究人员发现胆固醇药物辛伐他汀在夜间服用比白天服用更能有效降低胆固醇水平。这是因为这些药物靶向的肝酶 (酶) 在夜间更加活跃。

paragraphs.sourceText: Taking medicine at the wrong time can even cause harm. My colleagues and I wondered whether midazolam, the most common sedative (镇静剂) used in surgical procedures worldwide, might interfere with the internal clock that protects the heart at night. Currently, there are no guidelines regarding when midazolam should be administered.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在错误的时间服药甚至会造成伤害。我和我的同事想知道咪达唑仑（全世界外科手术中最常用的镇静剂）是否会干扰夜间保护心脏的生物钟。目前，尚无关于何时应使用咪达唑仑的指南。

paragraphs.sourceText: More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases. I believe taking drug timing into account could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide.
paragraphs.translationZh: 需要更多的研究来确定治疗不同疾病的最佳时间。我相信考虑用药时机有助于使治疗更有效，并帮助全世界更多的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser ( 理发师) about retirement plans. The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经济学教授凯瑟琳·亚伯拉罕 (Katharine Abraham) 正在与理发师谈论退休计划。这位经济学家表示，她计划继续工作，因为她愿意。美发师同意了，但原因不同：她需要钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: Both scenarios (情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s. Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这两种情况都导致美国 70 多岁的人口数量大幅增加。过去20年来，70多岁的美国人工作比例从不到10%上升到近15%。

paragraphs.sourceText: In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经济学家表示，除了人们变得更健康、寿命更长之外，财务方面的考虑，例如多年来实际工资的缓慢增长以及私营部门传统养老金的转变，也是人们推迟退休的一些原因。研究美国老年人的工作和退休决定的亚伯拉罕表示，制造业的衰落和从事劳动密集度较低的职业的人数增加也促成了这一趋势。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you’re doing,” Abraham says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 亚伯拉罕说：“哪个更重要取决于你迄今为止所做的工作类型。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor’s degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总体趋势正在影响所有不同教育程度的美国人，尽管百分比因类别而异。 2018年，拥有学士学位的美国人中70多岁工作的比例接近20%。对于高中及以下学历的人来说，70多岁工作的比例已上升至10%左右，而具有一定大学学历的人则处于中间位置，约为15%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men. He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. They’re also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 领导退休保障研究项目的经济学家马丁·尼尔·贝利 (Martin Neil Baily) 指出，辞职可能会导致孤立和孤独感，尤其是对男性而言。他认为，许多受过大学教育的工人选择留在劳动力市场更多是为了社会福利，而不是出于经济原因。他们也更有可能从事更喜欢工作的专业职业。

paragraphs.sourceText: Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.
paragraphs.translationZh: 贝利表示，与此同时，从事更多体力工作的工人可能更有可能期待退休，这表明那些留下来的人更有可能是出于经济原因而这样做。
